name: Sweet-chili chicken breast (spray-fried, 1 kg base)

source.author: mako.co.il — 5-ingredient chicken breast in sweet chili sauce
source.notes: mako is egress-blocked by the network proxy, so the recipe was reconstructed from the identical 5-ingredient version (chicken dredged in flour, fried, tossed in sweet chili + honey/silan + soy) confirmed via web search. Built to the user's spec: 1 kg chicken breast and OLIVE-OIL SPRAY for frying instead of the original 4–5 tbsp of oil — that swap alone saves roughly 500 kcal / ~55 g fat off the whole dish. Analyzed for the whole batch; per_serving = batch ÷ 4. The sauce (sweet chili + soy) is the sugar/sodium lever. Estimate — sweet-chili sauces vary.

serving_desc: ≈220 g cooked (¼ of a 1 kg-chicken batch) — ~250 g raw chicken per serving

ingredients.note: whole-grain dredge — a little fiber vs white; shake off excess
main added-sugar source; a low-sugar sweet chili cuts it a lot
low-sodium — roughly halves the sodium vs regular soy
the user's swap for 4–5 tbsp oil — big calorie save

steps: Cut the chicken; dredge lightly in whole spelt flour and shake off the excess.
Spray a pan with olive oil, heat, and fry the chicken on both sides until golden and cooked through.
Mix the sweet chili, honey/silan and low-sodium soy; pour into the pan and toss 1–2 min until the sauce coats the chicken and turns glossy. Serve.

batch_totals.note: Whole 1 kg-chicken dish, spray-fried, with low-sodium soy + whole spelt dredge. Deep-frying the original way (4–5 tbsp oil) would add ~500 kcal / ~55 g fat — the spray swap keeps total fat to ~29 g. Low-sodium soy roughly halves the salt (~2,800 mg batch vs ~4,600 with regular soy). The sweet chili + honey still carry ~91 g added sugar across the batch — the remaining lever.

him.verdict: With the low-sodium soy + whole spelt dredge this is now a rotation-worthy lean-protein dish: ~59 g protein per serving for ~448 kcal (~13 g protein per 100 kcal!), the olive-oil-spray swap keeps fat to just ~7 g/serving, and the low-sodium soy roughly halves the salt to ~700 mg/serving. Whole spelt makes the dredge whole-grain for a bit of fiber. The only thing between this and a 9 is the sweet-chili + honey glaze — still ~23 g added sugar/serving. Cut the sweet chili and skip the honey whenever you want the cleaner version.
flags: ~59 g protein / 448 kcal (~13 g protein per 100 kcal — outstanding)
spray-fried: only ~7 g fat/serving (vs ~2x calories deep-fried)
low-sodium soy: ~700 mg sodium/serving (~halved vs regular soy)

suggested_mods: For a 9: halve the sweet chili + skip the honey (or use a low-sugar sweet chili) — the chili flavor still carries; drops added sugar sharply
Add garlic/ginger/chili flakes for flavor so you lean less on the sweet glaze
Bulk it with stir-fried veg (peppers, broccoli, snap peas) — adds fiber + vitamin C and stretches the servings
Keep the olive-oil spray + low-sodium soy — those swaps are doing the heavy lifting

her_preconception.verdict: Lean, fully-cooked chicken is a solid protein + choline + selenium source for her with no safety flags — cook it through (74 °C, no pink) as standard. The low-sodium soy meaningfully eases the salt (helpful in pregnancy) and the whole spelt adds a little folate/iron. The sweet-chili + honey glaze is still sugar-heavy, so keep the sauce modest and serve over vegetables for folate + vitamin C.

safety_advisories.note: Cook the chicken fully through (74 °C / no pink) — standard.

suggested_mods: Use low-sodium soy and less sweet chili to ease salt + sugar
Serve over a big veg/leafy side for folate, iron + vitamin C

adopted_note: Adopted 2026-09-25 with low-sodium soy + whole spelt dredge. Per serving (batch of 4, ~250 g raw chicken each): ~448 kcal, 59 g protein, 33 g carb, 7 g fat, ~700 mg sodium, ~23 g added sugar. him 8 / her 7. Spray-fry with olive oil (not deep-fry). Standing note: the sweet chili + honey are the remaining sugar lever — cut the sweet chili / skip the honey for a cleaner ~9 version; serve over veg for fiber + vitamin C.
cooking_guide: Cut the chicken into even strips or cubes so they cook at the same rate. Pat them DRY with paper towel and season with salt and pepper — dry surface is what lets them brown instead of steam.
Dredge lightly in whole spelt flour and shake off the excess for a thin whole-grain crust (or skip it for a lower-carb version).
Spray a nonstick pan with olive oil and heat over medium-high. Work in BATCHES — don't crowd the pan, or the chicken steams and goes grey instead of golden.
Sear the pieces undisturbed 2–3 min per side until deep golden and cooked through (74 °C, no pink). Set aside while you do the next batch.

Stir together the sweet chili, honey/silan and soy. Return all the chicken to the pan, pour the sauce over and toss 1–2 min on medium until it's glossy and clinging — don't go longer or the sugar scorches.
Finish with sesame and sliced scallions; serve over rice, noodles or stir-fried veg.

Lower sugar/sodium tips: use low-sodium soy, cut the sweet chili with a splash of water or rice vinegar, and lean on fresh garlic, ginger and chili flakes for flavor so you need less of the sweet glaze.
